title: High-Performance Clinician-in-the-Loop Deep Learning for Early Multi-Organ Pathology Detection
authors: Elena R. Vance, Kenji Takahashi, Marcus Holloway, Sarah Al-Mansoor
abstract: Automated diagnostic systems frequently suffer from domain shift and overconfidence when transitioning from laboratory benchmarks to heterogeneous clinical environments. Here we introduce MedNexus, a calibrated multi-modal foundation architecture that couples diffusion-guided vision transformers with interactive uncertainty maps. Evaluated across 142000 multi-institution scans MedNexus achieves an AUC-ROC of 0.984 for early thoracic malignancies while reducing false-positive biopsy referrals by 31.4 percent compared to standard radiological review protocols.
keywords: machine learning, medical diagnosis, radiology, computer vision, deep learning

title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning from Electronic Health Records for Rare Disease Trajectory Prediction
authors: Julian M. Thorne, Amina Diallo, Chen Wei, David O'Connor
abstract: Pre-symptomatic identification of rare metabolic and autoimmune conditions is severely bottlenecked by extreme class imbalance and fragmented longitudinal patient histories. We propose ChronoMed, a continuous-time neural ordinary differential equation framework trained with contrastive masking over 3.8 million de-identified electronic health records. Our findings demonstrate an average diagnostic lead-time advancement of 14.6 months prior to definitive clinical onset.
keywords: electronic health records, machine learning, medical diagnosis, representation learning, predictive modeling

title: Explainable Graph Neural Networks for Histopathology Whole-Slide Classification and Biomarker Discovery
authors: Sophia S. Lin, Gareth Evans, Maria Santos-Dumitrescu, Vikram Patel
abstract: Gigapixel whole-slide imaging presents unique computational hurdles for standard convolutional networks due to memory constraints and cellular hierarchy loss. In this paper we construct adaptive cell-interaction graphs where nodes denote nuclear morphometrics and edges encode microenvironment spatial proximity. Through hierarchical graph pooling and layer-wise relevance propagation our framework identifies novel morphological sub-clusters correlating with patient immunotherapy response.
keywords: graph neural networks, histopathology, machine learning, medical diagnosis, explainable ai

title: Benchmarking Foundation Models Against Board-Certified Radiologists in Complex Emergency Triage
authors: Arthur Pendelton, Zoya K. Varma, Lucas B. Meyer, Rachel Green
abstract: While multimodal vision-language models demonstrate impressive diagnostic accuracy on curated benchmarks their real-world utility in urgent triage scenarios remains insufficiently audited. We conduct a prospective double-blind trial comparing four frontier foundation models against 24 board-certified emergency radiologists across 5200 consecutive acute trauma cases. We observe notable strengths in localized pneumothorax detection alongside persistent blind spots in subtle cranial fractures.
keywords: foundation models, emergency medicine, medical diagnosis, radiology, benchmarking

title: Federated Continual Learning Across 18 Hospital Networks Without Centralized Data Sharing
authors: Henrik Lindqvist, Devon Ross, Fatima Zahra, Clara Schumann
abstract: Strict patient privacy regulations such as HIPAA and GDPR impede the consolidation of medical imaging repositories into centralized training facilities. We propose FedShield, a privacy-preserving federated distillation protocol with episodic memory consolidation to combat catastrophic forgetting during continuous clinical site onboarding. We validate continuous multi-organ oncology lesion segmentation across 18 hospital silos over two years without single raw data transmission.
keywords: federated learning, medical diagnosis, privacy, continual learning, healthcare systems

title: Acoustic Deep Learning Biomarkers for Non-Invasive Pulmonary Dysfunction Screening
authors: Naomi Campbell, Tariq Al-Fassi, Igor Stravinsky, Maya Lin
abstract: Point-of-care screening for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and interstitial lung disease remains difficult in resource-limited rural settings. We develop a smartphone-deployable acoustic convolutional model trained on 84000 auscultation audio waveforms captured in ambient conditions. Spectral attention modules isolate adventitious respiratory sounds from environmental noise with 94.2 percent diagnostic sensitivity.
keywords: acoustic biomarkers, signal processing, medical diagnosis, mobile health, machine learning

title: Attention Is All You Need: Scalable Multi-Head Self-Attention Architectures
authors: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit
abstract: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks. We propose the Transformer a novel network architecture based solely on attention mechanisms dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show superior quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less training time.
keywords: deep learning, attention mechanism, natural language processing, transformers

title: Fault-Tolerant Quantum Error Correction Below the Surface Code Threshold
authors: Evelyn Vance, Alexander Bohr, Devi Ramanujan, Siddharth Nair
abstract: Scaling quantum processors toward practical utility requires suppressing physical gate error rates below the fault-tolerant threshold. Here we demonstrate an 81-qubit planar transmon lattice implementing topological surface code error tracking across 25 consecutive error syndrome cycles. Physical noise is suppressed exponentially with code distance marking an operational milestone for logical qubit preservation.
keywords: quantum computing, surface codes, fault tolerance, error correction, quantum hardware

title: De Novo Macromolecular Structure Generation Using SE(3)-Equivariant Continuous Diffusion
authors: Camilla Rossi, Jean-Luc Moreau, Haruki Murakami, Anand Rao
abstract: Computational protein design has progressed from template-matching heuristics to generative geometric priors. We introduce FoldDiff an SE(3)-equivariant continuous diffusion model that generates backbone topologies and atomic coordinates jointly in continuous 3D Euclidean space. Laboratory synthesis confirms target binding affinity for 72 percent of computationally designed scaffolds against therapeutic viral epitopes.
keywords: diffusion models, protein design, geometric deep learning, structural biology

title: High-Density Intracortical Decoding of Natural Speech Intent at 90 Words Per Minute
authors: Sean O'Malley, Leticia Mendes, Nils Lindgren, Farah Kassem
abstract: Severe paralysis resulting from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis or brainstem stroke deprives individuals of expressive speech. We present a wireless 256-channel intracortical microelectrode array coupled to an autoregressive recurrent decoding pipeline capable of translating sub-vocal motor cortex firing patterns into phonemic sequences at 90.4 words per minute with 96.1 percent vocabulary accuracy.
keywords: brain-computer interface, neural decoding, machine learning, speech synthesis, neuroprosthetics

title: Uncertainty Quantification in Deep Bayesian Neural Networks for Dermatological Cancer Screening
authors: Claire Dupont, Liam Zhang, Aris Thorne, Mateo Silva
abstract: Reliable deployment of deep neural networks in oncology requires calibrated confidence bounds. We investigate Monte Carlo dropout and deep ensembles across 50000 dermoscopic skin lesion images. Our Bayesian framework correctly flags ambiguous borderline melanocytic lesions for secondary specialist dermatologist review, decreasing diagnostic misclassifications by 42 percent.
keywords: bayesian deep learning, dermatology, oncology, uncertainty quantification, medical diagnosis

title: Contrastive Learning for Cross-Modal Magnetic Resonance and Positron Emission Tomography Synthesis
authors: Hiroshi Tanaka, Maya Patel, Oliver Vance, Gabriel Costa
abstract: Multi-modal imaging is critical in neurodegenerative diagnosis but PET scans involve radioactive tracer injections and high cost. We propose CrossModalCL, a 3D generative diffusion pipeline with contrastive latent regularization that synthesizes synthetic amyloid PET scans directly from structural T1 MRI scans with structural similarity index of 0.92.
keywords: contrastive learning, magnetic resonance imaging, pet scan, multimodal ai, medical diagnosis

title: Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback for Clinical Communication and Diagnostic Explanation
authors: Beatrice Meyer, Samuel Green, Wei Liu, Ananya Rao
abstract: Physicians must convey complex medical prognoses empathetically and accurately. We train a 70-billion parameter clinical language model using reinforcement learning grounded in verified medical board rubric evaluations. In randomized trials involving simulated patient cohorts, clinicians rated model diagnostic explanations as more actionable than standard clinical summaries.
keywords: reinforcement learning, clinical communication, medical language models, medical diagnosis, rlhf

title: Zero-Shot Vision-Language Pretraining for Histopathology Phenotyping Across Diverse Demographics
authors: Nathaniel Cole, Zara Ahmed, Lucas Silva, Fiona Gallagher
abstract: Histopathological analysis often suffers from performance disparities across patient ethnicities due to biased training cohorts. We introduce HistoCLIP, trained on 1.2 million image-text pairs with demographic balancing loss. Zero-shot transfer achieves state-of-the-art diagnostic accuracy across 15 solid tumor types without retraining.
keywords: vision-language models, histopathology, zero-shot learning, demographic fairness, medical diagnosis

title: Graph Attention Networks for Drug Repurposing Against Antibiotic-Resistant Pathogens
authors: Dmitri Ivanov, Celine Laurent, Kevin O'Brien, Meera Joshi
abstract: The emergence of pan-drug resistant bacterial strains represents an escalating global public health emergency. Here we formulate molecular interaction networks as heterogeneous knowledge graphs and employ multi-relational graph attention to predict novel antibacterial affinities. Laboratory assays confirm potent bacteriostatic inhibition for three repurposed cardiovascular compounds.
keywords: graph neural networks, drug repurposing, antibiotic resistance, molecular networks, bioinformatics

title: Diffusion Probabilistic Models for 4D Cardiac MRI Motion Reconstruction
authors: Pauline Dubois, Marco Bellini, Svenja Keller, Rajiv Gupta
abstract: Cine-MRI of the heart suffers from breathing artifacts and acquisition duration trade-offs. We present a spatio-temporal continuous diffusion model that reconstructs high-resolution 4D myocardial strain tensors from undersampled k-space data, reducing MRI scan acquisition duration by 75 percent while preserving subtle left ventricular ejection abnormalities.
keywords: diffusion models, cardiac mri, image reconstruction, medical diagnosis, deep learning

title: Interpretable Survival Analysis Using Neural Proportional Hazards for Oncology Prognosis
authors: Eitan Katz, Laura Fernandez, Benjamin Cho, Seraphina Vance
abstract: Standard Cox proportional hazards models make restrictive linearity assumptions that fail to capture complex non-linear genomic-clinical interactions. We develop SurvNet, an additive neural architecture with neural spline hazard curves that guarantees individual feature interpretability while matching unrestricted multi-layer perceptron predictive accuracy across 32 cancer types.
keywords: survival analysis, oncology, interpretable machine learning, genomics, medical diagnosis

title: Quantum State Tomography via Compressed Sensing and Neural Tensor Networks
authors: Sora Takahashi, Liam O'Connor, Valeriya Morozova, Dirk Jansen
abstract: Characterizing high-dimensional entangled states in noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices demands exponential measurement scaling. We combine compressed sensing convex optimization with matrix product state neural decoders to reconstruct 20-qubit density matrices from only polynomial Pauli projections.
keywords: quantum computing, state tomography, tensor networks, compressed sensing, quantum physics

title: Global Climate Feedback Loop Modeling via Neural Earth System Emulators
authors: Helena Berg, Johannes Schmidt, Tariq Mansoor, Astrid Lindholm
abstract: Simulating coupled atmosphere-ocean-cryosphere dynamics requires months of compute on supercomputers. We construct ClimateSphere, a spherical Fourier neural operator that emulates 100-year planetary climate projections in 48 hours with fidelity comparable to CMIP6 ensemble models.
keywords: climate modeling, neural operators, earth system science, deep learning, planetary simulation

title: Causal Machine Learning for Estimating Heterogeneous Treatment Effects in Sepsis Resuscitation
authors: Gabriel Rossi, Emily Watson, Victor Adebayo, Charlotte Dubois
abstract: Determining optimal vasopressor and intravenous fluid timing in acute septic shock remains controversial in intensive care medicine. We apply double machine learning with causal trees to observational ICU data across 60000 patients, revealing distinct physiological phenotypes where early vasopressor initiation significantly reduces 28-day mortality.
keywords: causal inference, intensive care, sepsis, machine learning, medical diagnosis, treatment effect

title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback with Scalable Oversight
authors: Yuntao Bai, Saurav Kadavath, Amanda Askell, John Schulman, Dario Amodei
abstract: As AI models scale in reasoning capacity manual human feedback becomes inefficient and susceptible to human cognitive fatigue. We describe Constitutional AI a training paradigm using self-critique guided by a compact constitution of behavioral principles. We demonstrate that self-supervised AI reinforcement learning achieves superior harmlessness and refusal calibration without degrading task helpfulness across complex mathematical and code benchmarks.
keywords: artificial intelligence, ai alignment, reinforcement learning, large language models, safety

title: Digital Phenotyping and Longitudinal Wearable Sensing for Relapse Prediction in Major Depressive Disorder
authors: Talia R. Vance, Gabriel Morales, Amina Diallo, Thomas Insel
abstract: Major depressive disorder episodes are characterized by subtle neurovegetative shifts in sleep latency circadian rhythm fragmentation and voice prosody days prior to subjective symptom reporting. We deploy a multi-sensor mobile phenotyping platform tracking 1400 outpatients over 18 months. Continuous passive sensing paired with recurrent temporal graph networks forecasts depressive relapse episodes 11 days in advance with an AUC of 0.89.
keywords: mental health, digital phenotyping, psychiatry, wearable devices, depression

title: Zero-Knowledge Proofs and Rollup Scalability for Privacy-Preserving Instant Digital Payment Systems
authors: Vitalik Buterin, Eli Ben-Sasson, Zoe Cash, Vikram Seth
abstract: Central bank digital currencies and retail payment rails confront an inherent architectural tension between transaction throughput and consumer financial privacy. We construct zkPay a recursive STARK-based decentralized settlement pipeline capable of verifying 45000 retail transactions per second while cryptographically concealing payer balances and recipient identities from third-party intermediaries without sacrificing regulatory compliance.
keywords: digital payments, zero-knowledge proofs, fintech, cryptographic protocols, blockchain scalability

title: High-Resolution Neural Earth Emulators for Regional Extreme Weather and Carbon Cycle Dynamics
authors: Johannes Schmidt, Astrid Lindholm, Tariq Mansoor, Helena Berg
abstract: Accelerating planetary temperature anomalies demand localized forecasting of extreme precipitation tropical cyclogenesis and terrestrial carbon sequestration tipping points. We formulate ClimOperator an adaptive spherical Fourier neural operator trained on 40 years of ERA5 reanalysis data. Our emulator delivers 0.1-degree global forecasts at 10000x computational speedup relative to traditional fluid dynamics simulations.
keywords: climate change, earth system science, neural operators, extreme weather, carbon dynamics

title: Generative Multi-Agent Tutoring Architectures for Adaptive Mastery Learning in STEM Disciplines
authors: Maya Lin, Arthur Pendelton, Clara Schumann, Kenji Takahashi
abstract: Massive open online courses consistently experience student dropout rates exceeding 85 percent due to the absence of personalized pacing and interactive problem decomposition. We design CogniTutor an ensemble of collaborating LLM agents simulating pedagogical coaching cognitive diagnostic tracing and Socratic scaffolding. Across 12000 undergraduate engineering students CogniTutor boosted course completion by 44 percent.
keywords: online education, educational technology, adaptive learning, pedagogy, stem learning

title: Autonomous Threat Hunting and Zero-Day Binary Vulnerability Synthesis via Reinforcement Learning
authors: Dmitri Ivanov, Sarah Al-Mansoor, Devon Ross, Seraphina Vance
abstract: Critical infrastructure firmware faces automated adversary toolchains capable of polymorphic exploit generation. We introduce AegisNet a neuro-symbolic reinforcement learning environment that decompiles stripped binary control software models control-flow reachability lattices and autonomously patches memory corruption vulnerabilities before exploitation. Validated across 2000 Linux and RTOS binaries.
keywords: cybersecurity, vulnerability analysis, binary decompilation, reinforcement learning, network security
